name: Static var compensator
summary: A shunt reactive power compensator built from thyristor-controlled reactors, thyristor-switched capacitors and filters.
description: A static var compensator is a shunt-connected installation that controls voltage by rapidly varying the reactive power it exchanges with the network. Its branches are typically a thyristor-controlled reactor, one or more thyristor-switched capacitors and harmonic filters, all connected to the secondary of a dedicated step-down transformer.

Single-line diagrams show the compensator transformer feeding a medium-voltage bus with each branch drawn separately, or a summary block labelled SVC with a variable capacitor-reactor symbol. It is used at transmission substations, at large industrial loads such as arc furnaces and at some renewable connection points.

Because its output is based on switched reactances, available reactive current falls with voltage, so it gives less support during deep voltage dips than a STATCOM. The symbol does not show the control slope, the branch ratings or the harmonic performance.
readingNotes: Read each branch rating to find the inductive and capacitive range.
Filters in an SVC usually also supply part of the capacitive output.
drawingChecklist: State capacitive and inductive range in Mvar.
distinction: An SVC varies switched reactances; a STATCOM uses a voltage-source converter and holds output current better at low voltage.
